motivo: Todas las afirmaciones fácticas (salud/seguridad incluidas) coinciden con la página de Apple Support 'If your iPhone or iPad gets too hot or too cold' (https://support.apple.com/en-us/ht201678) y están atribuidas a Apple con el matiz correcto (might/could, temporarily). Unidades °F confirmadas: 0-35 °C = 32-95 °F. No hay afirmaciones falsas, dudosas ni sin fuente. Nota menor sin impacto: 'dies at 40%' es la premisa gancho (experiencia cotidiana), no una afirmación de dato; el guion no promete explicar el mecanismo.

afirmaciones.texto: Apple says iPhones are designed for temperatures between 32 and 95 °F (guion: thirty-two and ninety-five degrees Fahrenheit; guardable: 32 to 95 F)
afirmaciones.fuente: Apple Support, https://support.apple.com/en-us/ht201678: 'between 0º and 35º C (32º to 95º F)'

afirmaciones.texto: In very cold conditions, battery life can get temporarily shorter and the phone could shut itself off
afirmaciones.fuente: Apple Support, ht201678: 'might temporarily shorten battery life and could cause your device to turn off'
Apple Support, ht201678: 'might not charge or could stop charging'

afirmaciones.texto: Apple says battery life returns to normal when the phone gets back to higher temperatures
afirmaciones.fuente: Apple Support, ht201678: 'Battery life will return to normal when you bring your device back to higher ambient temperatures'

afirmaciones.texto: Apple also says not to leave your phone in a parked car, where the temperature can go outside that range
afirmaciones.fuente: Apple Support, ht201678: 'Don't leave your device in a car, because temperatures in parked cars can exceed this range'

afirmaciones.texto: Regla guardable: 'iPhones are designed for 32 to 95 F. Too cold: battery life can get shorter and it can shut off. Warm it up and battery life returns to normal.' / caption: 'very cold = shorter battery life or shutoff · warm back up = back to normal'
afirmaciones.fuente: Apple Support, ht201678 (resumen de los puntos anteriores)

afirmaciones.texto: Atribución y fuente citada: 'Apple Support (If your iPhone or iPad gets too hot or too cold)'
afirmaciones.fuente: Título de la página ht201678, confirmado
